meta.intro:
Thunder rattles the windows of Blackwood Manor. The lights failed at ten past nine, the road has flooded, and nobody is going anywhere tonight.

You were expected for dinner, but the storm had other ideas. Your motor stalled in the floodwater at the foot of the drive, and by the time you squelched up to the front door, at a quarter to ten, the lights were back on, the police had been telephoned and could not get through, and Lord Blackwood lay dead in his own locked library. The key is nowhere to be found.

The butler is polishing things that are already clean. The lady of the house keeps fainting. The business partner is shouting. The gardener won't look anyone in the eye. Grab your magnifying glass, detective: someone in this house is a murderer.
meta.tagline: A dark and stormy night. A locked library. Four suspects, and every one of them is hiding something.
meta.title: Murder at Blackwood Manor

evidence.discoveryLine: A boot print! Big, muddy, and pointing straight at the library door like an accusing finger.
evidence.name: Muddy Footprint

evidence.description: A charred letter on a solicitor's notepaper, found in the ashes of the dining-room fireplace. Legible fragments: '...the new will, drawn as you instructed, leaves Lady Victoria two hundred pounds a year and nothing further...'; '...I shall call at ten tomorrow for your signature...'; '...as to the household accounts, the discrepancies do point to your butler, and I advise an audit...'
evidence.discoveryLine: Rescued from the flames, only slightly toasted! Somebody wanted these words gone. Somebody failed.
evidence.name: Burned Letter

evidence.description: The only key to the library. When the door was forced it was not in the lock, not on his lordship and nowhere in the library. It turns up, sooty, at the bottom of the coal scuttle beside the dining-room hearth.
evidence.discoveryLine: A key at the bottom of the coal scuttle! Keys don't usually climb in there by themselves.
evidence.name: The Missing Library Key

locations.description: Lord Blackwood's book-lined sanctum at the end of the hall. One oak door to the hall with a single key; tall windows shuttered and bolted against the storm; a coal fire.
locations.name: The Library

searchFlavor.emptyLine: You re-check the shelves, the rug and the dead fire. Four thousand books, still not talking. Nothing new here.
lines: A dying fire, a splintered door and four thousand books that saw everything and aren't saying a word.
You tiptoe around his lordship's favourite rug. Somewhere, a violin plays one very ominous note.

locations.description: Long table, a pair of silver candlesticks and a roaring hearth.
locations.lockedLine: Crime scene first, detective! Procedure! Start where his lordship fell, and the dining room will still be here when you get back.
locations.name: The Dining Room

searchFlavor.emptyLine: You count the pudding bowls again. Still three. Still nobody finished the trifle. Nothing new here.
lines: Dinner for three, abandoned mid-pudding. A lone silver candlestick stands on the table, looking for its other half.
The fire has sulked down to embers, and the hearth wears the smug look of a fireplace that knows something.

locations.description: The manor's central hall joining every room. Tall windows, a grandfather clock, and a garden door with a dark alcove beside it.
locations.name: The Hall

searchFlavor.emptyLine: You stare at the portraits. The portraits stare back. The grandfather clock clears its throat. Nothing new here.
lines: The grandfather clock ticks, the thunder booms, and every portrait on the wall seems to be staring at the library door.
Doors in every direction, a draughty garden door that won't stop rattling, and puddles. Mind the puddles.

locations.description: Lawns, greenhouse and potting shed, lashed by the storm. The garden door leads into the hall; the kitchen door leads into the servants' quarters.
locations.name: The Garden

searchFlavor.emptyLine: You search the flowerbeds again and find mud, more mud, and a snail who refuses to answer questions. The lantern has told you all it is going to.
lines: Rain, mud, a sulking greenhouse and one extremely soggy scarecrow. The storm has rinsed away everything but the worms.
Beside the garden door lies a storm lantern, snuffed out and abandoned. Somebody came in out of the dark in a hurry, and left their light behind.

locations.description: Kitchen, the butler's pantry, and the manor's only telephone on the wall of the servants' passage.
locations.name: Kitchen & Servants' Quarters

searchFlavor.emptyLine: You check the bread bin, the biscuit tin and behind the mangle. Plenty of crumbs, nothing else to find.
lines: Copper pans gleam, a kettle grumbles on the range, and the whole place smells of boiled cabbage and nerves.
The servants' telephone hangs a little crooked on its hook, with a soggy shred of cigar stuck to the mouthpiece. Somebody has been chewing on their calls.

howToPlayTips: The road is flooded and nobody is leaving tonight. Whoever did it is still under this roof.
Question the staff as carefully as the family. Everyone at the manor is hiding something.
Not every secret here is about the murder. Plenty of people are lying for their own reasons.
The evening ran to the minute. Note every time you're given and check it against the others.
Search the rooms early, then come back: when a room shows ✨ Something new, search it again.
One suspect's confession can shake another's story loose. Show testimony to the others.
meta.intro:
Thunder rattles the windows of Blackwood Manor. The lights failed at ten past nine, the road has flooded, and nobody is going anywhere tonight.

You were expected for dinner, but the storm had other ideas. Your motor stalled in the floodwater at the foot of the drive, and by the time you squelched up to the front door, at a quarter to ten, the lights were back on, the police had been telephoned and could not get through, and Lord Blackwood lay dead in his own locked library. The key is nowhere to be found.

The butler is polishing things that are already clean. The lady of the house keeps fainting. The business partner is shouting. The gardener won't look anyone in the eye. Grab your magnifying glass, detective: someone in this house is a murderer.
meta.tagline: A dark and stormy night. A locked library. Four suspects, and every one of them is hiding something.
meta.title: Murder at Blackwood Manor

motives.description: Someone faced disgrace, or prison, if Lord Blackwood talked.
motives.label: Business ruin

motives.description: Someone stood to gain from Lord Blackwood's fortune.
motives.label: Inheritance

motives.description: Someone had a score to settle with his lordship.
motives.label: Revenge

motives.description: Someone had been quietly helping themselves, and his lordship was getting close.
motives.label: Stolen money

motives.description: Someone wanted to be free of Lord Blackwood, whatever it cost.
motives.label: Unhappy marriage

accuse.line: A hunch and a hat don't close a case, detective. Keep looking.

leads.hint: Somebody used something heavy. The library is where it happened, so that is where a tidy detective starts.
leads.title: What struck his lordship down?

leads.hint: Money, grudges and who-gets-what: somebody in this house is better off tonight. Find out what they were fighting over.
leads.title: Who gains from his death?

suspects.bio: Lord Blackwood's loud, cigar-chomping business partner, staying the night. Wears a waistcoat under considerable strain.
suspects.name: Archibald Crane

suspects.bio: The Blackwoods' gardener, sacked that very morning. Soaked, shaking, and not keen on talking.
suspects.name: Gregory

suspects.bio: Butler to the Blackwoods for twenty years, starched from collar to soul. Knows where every spoon is, and most of the secrets.
suspects.name: Reginald

suspects.bio: Lord Blackwood's elegant wife, now his widow. Famous for her parties, her pearls and her fainting spells, which are always perfectly timed.
suspects.name: Victoria Blackwood

victim.causeOfDeath: A single heavy blow to the head. His monocle is still in shock.
victim.description: Master of Blackwood Manor: rich, sharp-tongued and famously hard to please. Everyone in the house owed him something, and he never let them forget it.
victim.name: Lord Blackwood
